events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 18%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 1,529 to 1,261 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.

events.title: Structural Adjustment Programme
events.detail: Nigeria adopted a programme devaluing the naira through a second-tier foreign exchange market, cutting subsidies and dismantling commodity marketing boards.
events.contested: A standard reference case in the debate over 1980s structural adjustment in Africa. Defenders point to unsustainable pre-reform distortions; critics point to falling real wages, the collapse of social spending and the absence of the promised supply response.
events.refs: ["Federal Government of Nigeria, Structural Adjustment Programme 1986-88"]

events.title: Inflation crossed 50% (reached 55%)
events.detail: Consumer price inflation rose from 11.3% to 54.5%, crossing the 50% threshold.
events.source: derived: World Bank consumer price inflation
events.contested: The 50% line is a convention, not a natural boundary. Official inflation statistics are also among the most manipulated numbers governments publish, so the true figure may be higher than the one recorded here.

events.title: Democratic opening: electoral democracy index rose 0.28 over 5 years
events.detail: From 0.19 in 1995 to 0.47 in 2000. Derived by detecting a sustained shift of at least 0.2 index points over 5 years; marked at the steepest year of the episode.
events.contested: V-Dem indices are aggregated expert judgements with published uncertainty intervals. A shift of this size is well outside the noise, but the exact year is a property of the detection rule, not a documented event.
